assessments.reasoning: The survey instrument allows distinguishing de jure from de facto female-headed households because marital status (Bloque IV Col 07) combined with sex (Col 04) and the presence or absence of a partner/spouse in the household roster (Col 03) can separate unpartnered female heads (de jure) from partnered female heads whose spouse is absent (de facto). Women-maintained households can be identified through the main economic provider regardless of who is designated as head, because individual-level labor income (Individual Questionnaire Bloque 8d) and non-labor income (Household Questionnaire Bloque VI) are assigned to specific individual household components. Conversely, unpartnered mother-child units inside larger extended households cannot be identified because relationship to head (Col 03) is coded solely relative to the household head without person pointers to identify parent-child ties among non-head members. Finally, mother-child units cannot be linked to their own consumption, production, or care activity because activities such as domestic work (Bloque VII) are only captured at the aggregate household level.
